# SQLx connection-return patch

**WARNING: This is a temporary vendored backport of an unmerged upstream fix, not an upstream release. TODO: Replace it as soon as [SQLx PR #4350](https://github.com/transact-rs/sqlx/pull/4350) is merged, using an exact upstream Git revision containing the fix and the validation steps below.**

This directory contains the crates.io `sqlx-core` 0.9.0 source, with its original MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses. The published license-file links are expanded to the actual license texts from upstream revision `003b698e99e024f3621b8043a2426fde5b741171`. The normalized published `Cargo.toml` is used unchanged; `Cargo.toml.orig` and `.cargo_vcs_info.json` preserve upstream provenance. The registry package's lockfile and Cargo cache marker are not needed here.

The only upstream source change is in `src/pool/connection.rs`: the connection-return operation has a five-second deadline covering callbacks, ping and close. This backports the source change from [SQLx PR #4350](https://github.com/transact-rs/sqlx/pull/4350), revision `60772eb39474136adb15c6ffd68ded307649bc35`. That proposal is not merged as of 2026-11-04. On timeout, dropping the operation closes the local connection and releases its pool permit; normal return and minimum-connection maintenance retain their existing behavior.

Without this bound, cancelling a MySQL operation while the server is waiting for a lock can strand the pool permit, exhaust capacity and prevent application shutdown. A timeout only around an application `after_release` callback is insufficient because SQLx's subsequent close can also block. See [SQLx issue #4349](https://github.com/transact-rs/sqlx/issues/4349) and the related [TLS close report #4449](https://github.com/transact-rs/sqlx/issues/4449).

Ruphish tests this through its actual provider facade using a single-connection pool, verified TLS and a server-observed lock barrier in `crates/ruphish-adapters/tests/support/provider_regressions.rs`. No database reply or successful write is fabricated. The regression fails with the unmodified published crate.

Once the PR is merged, replace the path-based crates.io patch with `git` and an exact `rev` pointing to an upstream commit containing the fix. Review that revision's changes and compatibility with the remaining SQLx crates, and add a narrowly scoped exception for the upstream Git source in `deny.toml`. Update the lockfile through Cargo and rerun the cancellation regressions, supported provider suites and dependency-policy checks. Then remove this directory and its workspace exclusion; remove the `vendor/**` CI input group if no vendored dependencies remain. When a compatible SQLx release includes the fix, return to crates.io and remove the Git patch and source exception.
